Practical food ideas and nutrient sources
Content reviewed 6 October 2026. These are food ideas and source references, with no treatment or dosage advice. Ingredient filtering cannot guarantee allergy safety.
Calcium sources: milk, yogurt and cheese; some calcium-fortified plant drinks and tofu. Check the product label.
Iron sources include lentils, beans and some leafy vegetables. A varied diet can include these alongside other foods.
Vitamin C sources include citrus fruit, kiwi, peppers and broccoli.
References: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements consumer fact sheets for Calcium, Iron and Vitamin C; ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024).
Plain curd or a suitable alternative; washed seasonal fruit such as banana, orange or guava.
Cut the fruit and combine with the accompaniment you prefer. Adjust ingredients and portions; check labels for any dietary restriction.
Cooked beans, bread or another grain, optional sliced vegetables.
Warm the cooked beans if desired and serve with bread and vegetables. Change the ingredients to suit your available food.
Your safely stored cooked grain, dal or beans, and vegetables.
Follow the storage and reheating guidance appropriate to your ingredients. Assemble what you have and edit this idea for your usual meals.
Cooked lentils, cooked rice or another grain, seasonal vegetables, optional yogurt or lemon.
Use your usual cooked ingredients. Assemble the grain, lentils and vegetables; add the optional accompaniment you prefer. Adjust ingredients and portions to your needs.
